# Epistle of Barnabas — Chapter 15 (EMET Literal)

**Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Epistle of Barnabas 15
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

1. Moreover concerning the Sabbath it has also been written in the Ten Words in which he spoke to Moses face to face on Mount Sinai: "Hallow also the Sabbath of the Lord with pure hands and a pure heart."
2. And in another place he says: "If my sons keep the Sabbath, then I will bestow my mercy upon them."
3. The Sabbath is mentioned at the beginning of the creation: "And God made the works of his hands in six days, and he finished on the seventh day and rested on it and hallowed it."
4. Take note, children, what "he finished in six days" means. This means: in six thousand years the Lord will bring all things to an end; for a day with him represents a thousand years, and he himself testifies, saying: "Behold, the day of the Lord shall be as a thousand years." Therefore, children, in six days — that is, in six thousand years — all things will be brought to an end.
5. "And he rested on the seventh day." This means: when his Son comes, he will put an end to the time of the Lawless One, and will judge the ungodly, and will change the sun and the moon and the stars, and then he will truly rest on the seventh day.
6. Furthermore he says: "You shall hallow it with clean hands and a pure heart." If therefore anyone now is able to make holy that day which God has made holy, being pure in heart, we are deceived altogether.
7. Behold therefore we shall truly rest and make it holy then, when we ourselves shall be able to do so, having been made righteous and having received the promise — when there is no more lawlessness, and all things have been made new by the Lord. Then we shall be able to make it holy, having been made holy ourselves.
8. Furthermore he says to them: "Your new moons and the sabbaths I cannot endure." You see what he means: it is not the present sabbaths that are acceptable to me, but that which I have made, in which, when I have rested all things, I will make the beginning of the eighth day — that is, the beginning of another world.
9. For this reason also we celebrate the eighth day with joy — the day on which Jesus rose from the dead, and when he appeared, he ascended into the heavens.
